meta.note: Reference geometry in SOURCE-IMAGE pixels, exactly as measured in dist/dashboard-visual/measurements.json. compare.mjs subtracts the activity bar width to get webview coordinates. Each field is optional: only the edges present are compared.
meta.fontTolerance: Text anchors compare the glyph advance box, not the ink box: x is trustworthy, width is ±1 per glyph, and the y is a line box (above the ink), so y is reported but not gated.
meta.method: PowerShell 5.1 + System.Drawing edge detection over the reference PNG; ±1px on edges, ±1.5px on font sizes.

anchors.name: project.row.1
anchors.note: x0/x1 re-measured with the luminance probe: the list box's border spans image x900..1508 (card 885..1523, so a 14-15px inset both sides). The earlier 891 came from a noise band at luma 26-28.

anchors.name: tab.project.active
anchors.note: 5px, not 3: a tab's width is its label's advance, and 'Claude (8)' is ten glyphs — the fixture's own font rule allows ±1 per glyph. The strip's right edge (the thing a padding change moves) is exact.

anchors.name: tab.skills.active
anchors.note: x0/x1 re-measured with the luminance probe: the active tab's border spans image x277..375 (99 wide), not 290..419 — the earlier x1 caught the neighbouring tab's border.

anchors.name: activity.time.1
anchors.note: x1 是重新用亮度探针量的：参考图两行时间的右端同在 image x1166（左列那一栏），不是 1083——那个值量到的是一段空白。时间靠列右边缘对齐，所以它是列宽的证据，不是字体的事：列宽一错，整列时间跟着错。

anchors.name: activity.time.2
anchors.note: 右列时间实测右端 image x1490，比它自己那一列的横线末端（1508）内收 18px，而左列只内收 12px；我们两列都按 12px 排，于是这里差约 6px。报告给眼睛看，不做门。

anchors.name: brand.mark.ink
anchors.note: The mark is an with transparent padding, so the harness measures the RENDERED ink through a canvas, not the element box.

anchors.name: head.shared.title
anchors.note: Scoped to .cards-row: an unscoped .card-head .card-title index 0 also matches the Agent Configuration panel's own head, which sits higher up the page. Titles are drawn with a different icon set than the reference's, so 8px is the honest bound.

anchors.name: head.quick.title
anchors.note: index 1: the compact heads are Skills (0) and Quick Actions (1).

anchors.name: text.field.label.1
anchors.note: The Claude card's first field row ('Authentication'). Ink measured with the luminance probe over image x313..470 y215..250: the label run starts at 320, right after the field icon (ink 288..301) — the 18px between them is the row's own gap, not a font artefact.

anchors.name: text.agent.ready.1
anchors.note: The status pill's words ('Ready'), not the dot: the dot is a separate span at 347..357 and the run after it starts at 366.

anchors.name: config.btn.claude
anchors.note: The card's foot button ('Open Config File ↗'). Borders found by scanning row y447 (left border 284..286, right 444..446) and column x440 (top 437, bottom 464): a 163x28 box.

anchors.name: text.skill.desc.1
anchors.note: The description run starts 2px after the name run's box ends (318..410), i.e. the name column is a fixed width, not a gap.

anchors.name: skills.marks.1
anchors.note: The three agent marks on the first skill row: ink 657..731 with the middle one (Codex) white and the outer two tinted.

anchors.name: skills.pill.1
anchors.note: The 'Enabled' pill's own box (border to border), found on row y872: left border 751, right 817, with the state dot at 765 and the mint label after it.

structure.name: sidebar.present
structure.note: The reference's leftmost column is the dashboard's own sidebar (image x45..247), not VS Code's activity bar: without it every other measurement describes a layout that is not on screen.

structure.name: sidebar.width
structure.note: The reference's sidebar band is image x45..246 inclusive — 202px of webview once the 45px activity bar is subtracted — and the stylesheet's own token is 203. ±3 accepts the token and the band's own ±1 measurement error and still refuses any change that moves the panel by 4px or more.

structure.name: sidebar.nav.items
structure.note: The reference draws six destinations (the active band at y89 and text.nav.6's run at y310 are the first and the last): Overview, Configure, Agents, Sessions, Skills, Quick Actions.

structure.name: sidebar.nav.sections
structure.note: Six items in the reference's order. The order is part of the structure: the section list is a reading order, and the same six in another order is a different sidebar.

structure.name: sidebar.active.count
structure.note: One destination is the one being shown. Two highlighted entries (or none) tell the reader two different things about where they are.

structure.name: sidebar.active.section
structure.note: The reference screenshot is the Overview, and its first nav item carries the active band — so the active entry is Overview, read back from the markup rather than from the flag the harness passed in.

structure.name: sidebar.brand.mark
structure.note: The brand mark is an ; 'present' means the file resolved (naturalWidth > 0), not that a box exists. A broken src keeps the box and would pass a rect test.

structure.name: sidebar.footer.version
structure.note: The footer reads 'Avenic v<version>', where the version is the CLI the reader is running — live machine data, and on another machine than this one it is a different dotted number. So the pattern is fatal and the digits are not: a footer reading 'Avenic', 'Version 9' or 'Avenic vNext' fails this gate, while 'Avenic v1.8.3' against this fixture's 1.8.4 passes and is printed in the JSON (rows[].measured) so the drift is still visible. The footer's own box is anchored by text.version.

structure.name: header.present
structure.note: The project header and its five parts: title, root, configured pill, Refresh, Reconfigure. The reference's header band is image x262..1523 y0..73.

structure.name: header.title.matchesPayload
structure.note: The heading prints the project this payload names. Compared against the payload rather than against a string, so the gate fails when the renderer stops printing data and not when a fixture's project is renamed.

structure.name: header.configured.matchesPayload
structure.note: 'Avenic Configured' or 'Not Configured' has to agree with the payload's own answer: the pill is the one place the header states it, and the wrong word there is the panel contradicting core.

structure.name: header.refresh
structure.note: The reference's header carries a labelled Refresh control (image x1254..1363); it is the one header action that is not Reconfigure.

structure.name: header.height
structure.note: The reference's header band is y0..73, 74px. Already anchored edge by edge with tol 1; this gate states the structural fact so a second header-shaped row cannot take its place.

structure.name: agents.cards
structure.note: Agent Configuration is three cards in the reference (Claude, Codex, OpenCode).

structure.name: agents.row
structure.note: At the reference width the three cards sit on one row (all three tops within 2px), which is the 'three equal cards' the reference draws rather than a column of three.

structure.name: agents.order
structure.note: Read off each card's own mark, so a reordered or dropped card shows here even when the grid still holds three boxes.

structure.name: agents.heightSpread
structure.note: The reference's three cards are the same height (its first spans y148..468). Tolerance 2 is the drawing's own edge error; a card growing a row taller than its siblings is a structural change.

structure.name: sessions.cards
structure.note: Shared Sessions and Agent Sessions, the pair the reference draws at y494..748. The right-hand card was renamed from the reference's own wording on 2026-09-23 — the picture is unchanged, so the two anchor boxes above still gate this row and only the title string moved.

structure.name: sessions.columns
structure.note: Two columns at the reference width, not a stack: measured as two distinct left edges in that row. A list row inside the card cannot be read in a card that folded to half width.

structure.name: sessions.titles
structure.note: Left card first. The titles are the only thing on the page that says which history a list belongs to, so they are gated as the words a reader sees rather than as a count of cards. The product terms are Shared Sessions and Agent Sessions (2026-09-23); the reference screenshot's own right-hand title, which this build no longer prints, is in the note above.

structure.name: bottom.cards
structure.note: Skills, Quick Actions and Recent Activity: three cards in the reference's second row, with the last two stacked in its right-hand column.

structure.name: bottom.columns
structure.note: Skills on the left, the Quick Actions / Recent Activity stack on the right — the reference's x263..873 and x886..1523.

structure.name: skills.present
structure.note: The Skills card is the reference's own card (x263..873 y758..1012) rather than any card that happens to sit there.

structure.name: quick.present
structure.note: Quick Actions is the reference's third row (x886..1523 y758..906), and its grid is 3 wide by 2 tall.

structure.name: quick.buttons
structure.note: Six actions in the reference's grid (quick.button.1 and quick.button.4 are its first and fourth cells).

structure.name: quick.rows
structure.note: Two grid rows: the reference's buttons sit at y813..850 and y857..894, so a single row of six would not be this layout.

structure.name: sections.order
structure.expect: Agent Configuration | Shared Sessions | Agent Sessions | Skills | Quick Actions | Recent Activity
structure.note: The order the overview stacks its sections in, read off the rendered document. Every card can be in the right place and the page still read differently if two of them swap.

structure.name: grid.sessions.topDelta
structure.note: The two session cards are one band: their top edges may not disagree by more than the drawing's own error. Read off the rendered boxes, not the stylesheet — two cards with the same declared height can still be laid out apart.

structure.name: grid.sessions.bottomDelta
structure.note: And their bottom edges are the one the eye reads as tidy or ragged: a card that ends where its own list ended leaves the pair with a step in it. The reference's own pair is 1px apart (its shared card measures y747 against its project card's y748), so 2 is the tolerance and the reference is inside it.

structure.name: grid.bottom.topDelta
structure.note: Skills against Quick Actions: the second row's two columns start together.

structure.name: grid.bottom.bottomDelta
structure.note: And they end together, which is the whole of 'the right-hand stack is as tall as the card beside it'. The reference draws it: its Skills card spans y758..1012 and its Recent Activity y916..1011 — one 253px band in two pieces.

structure.name: grid.bottom.fillDelta
structure.note: The inside of that column: Recent Activity has to reach the bottom of the stack it is the last card of. Without this, both columns can end together while the stack still has a hole under it — measured 0 on this render, and 73px on a payload whose skills card was the shorter one before the row was stretched.

structure.name: brand.token
structure.note: The accent colour sampled from the reference's own orange. Gated separately from the two painted values below because a token nothing applies is not a colour on screen.

structure.name: brand.navActive.rgb
structure.note: The active nav item's glyph, as painted. Tolerance 4 per channel is under the smallest visible step between the reference's orange and a neighbouring hue (#e2651c is 25 away in red).

structure.name: brand.primary.rgb
structure.note: The primary button's fill — the reference's Reconfigure — which is the largest area of brand colour on screen.

structure.name: keyCards.count
structure.note: How many blocks the viewport gate below measured: sidebar, header, the Agent Configuration panel, the two session cards, Skills, Quick Actions and Recent Activity. Pinned so that 'nothing is outside the window' cannot pass by measuring nothing.

structure.name: keyCards.outside
structure.note: No key card may be painted where only a sideways scroll (or nothing at all) could reach it: left of the viewport, past its right edge, above the page, or past the page's own scrollable bottom.

structure.name: overflow.page
structure.note: The page itself must not scroll sideways — the reference is a fixed-width window whose content fits it.

structure.name: overflow.fits
structure.note: The vertical half of the gate above, and the half a screenshot cannot state: this window's document is exactly as tall as its viewport (scrollHeight 1024 in 1024), which is what 'the Overview is full to the bottom edge' means in numbers. A page can look full in a picture and still be scrolled, so the same fact is also gated on the 16:9 runs that declare fits. See shot.mjs's fits check and overflow.fits in its structure table.

structure.name: overflow.spilled
structure.note: And no element may be laid out past the window's edge — a box a non-root ancestor holds is still reported and the string names the holder, because content that wants more width than its container is the same defect one step earlier; the page root is never accepted as the holder. See shot.mjs's 'spilled' check.

structure.name: overflow.clippedCandidates
structure.note: The size of the set shot.mjs's clipped-text check measured on this render. Pinned because the check walks a fixed selector list: renamed classes empty the set, zero candidates fail zero times, and the check goes green forever. This number moves when the markup legitimately changes; it must never move because the gate stopped looking.
